title.en: Volume 123 Biographies 48: Li, Xiao, Lu, Wei, Zhao, He
title.raw: 卷一百二十三 列傳第四十八 李蕭盧韋趙和 Volume 123 Biographies 48: Li, Xiao, Lu, Wei, Zhao, He

sentences.zh: 李蕭盧韋趙和

translations.literal: Li, Xiao, Lu, Wei, Zhao, and He
translations.idiomatic: Li, Xiao, Lu, Wei, Zhao, and He

sentences.zh: ◎李蕭盧韋趙和

translations.literal: ◎ Li, Xiao, Lu, Wei, Zhao, and He
translations.idiomatic: Li, Xiao, Lu, Wei, Zhao, and He

sentences.zh: 李嶠，字巨山，趙州贊皇人。

translations.literal: Li Qiao, styled Jushan, was a man of Zanhuang in Zhao Prefecture.
translations.idiomatic: Li Qiao, courtesy name Jushan, was a native of Zanhuang in Zhao Prefecture.

sentences.zh: 早孤，事母孝。

translations.literal: He lost his father early and served his mother with filial devotion.
translations.idiomatic: Orphaned young, he served his mother with exemplary filial devotion.

sentences.zh: 為兒時，夢人遺雙筆，自是有文辭，十五通《五經》，薛元超稱之。

translations.literal: As a child he dreamed that someone gave him a pair of brushes; from then on he had literary talent. At fifteen he mastered the Five Classics, and Xue Yuanchao praised him.
translations.idiomatic: In childhood he dreamed that someone presented him with a pair of writing brushes; thereafter he showed literary gifts. At fifteen he had mastered the Five Classics, and Xue Yuanchao spoke highly of him.

sentences.zh: 二十擢進士第，始調安定尉。

translations.literal: At twenty he passed the jinshi examination and was first appointed magistrate of Anding.
translations.idiomatic: At twenty he passed the jinshi examination and was first posted as magistrate of Anding.

sentences.zh: 舉制策甲科，遷長安。

translations.literal: He passed the policy examination in the top grade and was transferred to Chang'an.
translations.idiomatic: He took the policy examination in the highest grade and was transferred to Chang'an.

sentences.zh: 時畿尉名文章者，駱賓王、劉光業，嶠最少，與等夷。

translations.literal: At that time the metropolitan magistrates famed for literary writing were Luo Binwang and Liu Guangye; Qiao was the youngest yet ranked as their equal.
translations.idiomatic: The capital magistrates then most famed for literary skill were Luo Binwang and Liu Guangye; Qiao was the youngest yet stood on equal footing with them.

sentences.zh: 授監察御史。

translations.literal: He was appointed investigating censor.
translations.idiomatic: He was appointed investigating censor.

sentences.zh: 高宗擊邕、巖二州叛獠，詔監其軍，嶠入洞喻降之，由是罷兵。

translations.literal: When Emperor Gaozong attacked the rebel Liao of Yong and Yan prefectures, he ordered Qiao to oversee the army; Qiao entered the caves to persuade them to submit, whereupon the troops were withdrawn.
translations.idiomatic: When Emperor Gaozong campaigned against rebel tribes in Yong and Yan prefectures, Qiao was ordered to supervise the army; he entered their mountain strongholds to persuade surrender, and the campaign was then halted.

sentences.zh: 稍遷給事中。

translations.literal: He was gradually promoted to attendant in the Office of the Censorate.
translations.idiomatic: He was soon promoted to attendant in the Office of the Censorate.

sentences.zh: 會來俊臣構狄仁傑、李嗣真、裴宣禮等獄，將抵死，敕嶠與大理少卿張德裕、侍御史劉憲覆驗，德裕等內知其冤，不敢異。

translations.literal: When Lai Junchen fabricated cases against Di Renjie, Li Sizhen, Pei Xuanli, and others, who were about to be executed, an edict ordered Qiao, together with Vice Director of the Court of Judicial Review Zhang Deyu and investigating censor Liu Xian, to re-examine the cases. Deyu and the others knew inwardly of their innocence but dared not dissent.
translations.idiomatic: When Lai Junchen framed Di Renjie, Li Sizhen, Pei Xuanli, and others in capital cases nearing execution, an edict sent Qiao, Vice Director Zhang Deyu of the Court of Judicial Review, and Investigating Censor Liu Xian to review the verdicts. Zhang and Liu knew the men were innocent but dared not disagree.

sentences.zh: 嶠曰：「知其枉不申，是謂見義不為者。

translations.literal: Qiao said: "To know they are wronged yet not speak up is what is called seeing righteousness and not acting."
translations.idiomatic: Qiao said, "To know they have been wronged and yet not speak out is what the sages call seeing what is right and failing to act."

sentences.zh: 」卒與二人列其枉，忤武後旨，出為潤州司馬。

translations.literal: In the end he and the other two listed their wrongful treatment, offending Empress Wu's intention, and he was sent out as secretary in Run Prefecture.
translations.idiomatic: In the end he and the other two set forth how the men had been wronged, defying Empress Wu's wishes; he was demoted to secretary in Run Prefecture.

sentences.zh: 久乃召為鳳閣舍人，文冊大號令，多主為之。

translations.literal: After a long while he was summoned back as aide in the Phoenix Pavilion, and most of the great proclamations and documents were drafted by him.
translations.idiomatic: After a long interval he was recalled as aide in the Phoenix Pavilion, and most of the court's major edicts and documents were drafted under his hand.

sentences.zh: 初置右御史臺，察州縣吏善惡、風俗得失，嶠上疏曰：「禁網上疏，法象宜簡，簡則法易行而不煩雜，疏則所羅廣而不苛碎。

translations.literal: When the Right Censorate was first established to inspect the good and evil of prefectural and county officials and the gains and losses of local custom, Qiao submitted a memorial saying: "The prohibitory net should be loose above and strict below; legal forms should be simple—if simple, the law is easy to enforce without confusion; if loose above, what it covers is broad without petty fragmentation."
translations.idiomatic: When the Right Censorate was first set up to examine the conduct of prefectural and county officials and the strengths and failings of local custom, Qiao submitted a memorial: "The law's reach should be broad above and precise below; its forms should be kept simple—simplicity makes enforcement easy and avoids confusion, while breadth of scope covers much without petty nitpicking."

sentences.zh: 伏見垂拱時，諸道巡察使科條四十有四，至別敕令又三十。

translations.literal: I observe that in the Chuigong era the touring inspectors of the circuits had forty-four articles of regulation, and separate edicts added thirty more.
translations.idiomatic: I note that under the Chuigong reign the circuit touring inspectors already had forty-four regulatory articles, with thirty more added by separate edicts.

sentences.zh: 而使以三月出，盡十一月奏事，每道所察吏，多者二千，少亦千計，要在品核才行而褒貶之。

translations.literal: Yet the envoys set out in the third month and had to finish reporting by the eleventh; in each circuit the officials inspected numbered as many as two thousand or no fewer than a thousand—the aim being to grade talent and conduct for praise or blame.
translations.idiomatic: Yet envoys were sent out in the third month and had to file reports by the eleventh; each circuit involved as many as two thousand officials under review, or no fewer than a thousand—all to be graded on talent and conduct for commendation or censure.

sentences.zh: 今期會迫促，奔逐不暇，欲望詳究所能，不亦艱哉。

translations.literal: Now deadlines press close and envoys rush about without respite—how can one hope to examine each man's capacity in detail? Is this not arduous?
translations.idiomatic: With deadlines so tight and envoys racing without pause, how can they hope to examine each man's capacity in full? The task is plainly beyond reach.

sentences.zh: 此非隳於職，才有限，力不逮耳。

translations.literal: This is not failure of duty but limitation of talent—the strength simply does not suffice.
translations.idiomatic: This is not dereliction of duty but the limits of human capacity—men simply cannot do more.

sentences.zh: 臣願量其功程以為節制，使器周於用，力濟於時，然後得失可以精核矣。

translations.literal: Your servant wishes to measure their tasks and set limits, so that capacity matches use and effort meets the time—only then can gains and losses be examined with precision.
translations.idiomatic: I ask that their workload be measured and bounded, so that capacity matches the task and effort fits the season—only then can results be judged with precision.

sentences.zh: 」又言：「今所察按，準漢六條而推廣之，則無不包矣，烏在多張事目也？

translations.literal: He also said: "What is now inspected and prosecuted, if measured by the Han six articles and extended, would embrace everything—why multiply categories of matters?"
translations.idiomatic: He added: "If inspection followed the Han six articles and their extensions, nothing would lie outside their scope—why multiply categories of charges?"

sentences.zh: 且朝廷萬機非無事，而機事之動，常在四方，故出使者冠蓋相望。

translations.literal: Moreover the court's myriad affairs are not without business, and when urgent matters arise they are often in the four quarters—hence envoys' carriages and canopies follow one another.
translations.idiomatic: The court's myriad affairs are never idle, and when urgent business arises it is usually in the provinces—hence the endless stream of traveling envoys.

sentences.zh: 今已置使，則外州之事悉得專之，傳驛減矣。

translations.literal: Now that inspectors are in place, outer prefectures' affairs can all be entrusted to them, and relay traffic is reduced.
translations.idiomatic: With permanent inspectors in place, provincial affairs can be entrusted to them alone, and relay traffic is cut down.

sentences.zh: 請率十州置一御史，以期歲為之限，容其身到屬縣，過閭裏，督察奸訛，采風俗，然後可課其成功。

translations.literal: I ask that one censor be set for every ten prefectures, with a term of one year, allowing him to reach subordinate counties in person, pass through hamlets, investigate fraud and error, gather local custom, and only then assess his success.
translations.idiomatic: I propose one censor for every ten prefectures, with a one-year term, time enough to reach subordinate counties in person, walk the lanes, investigate fraud, observe local custom, and only then judge his results.

sentences.zh: 且御史出入天禁，勵己自脩，比他吏相百也。

translations.literal: Moreover censors enter and leave the heavenly precincts and discipline themselves in self-cultivation—a hundred times more than other officials.
translations.idiomatic: Censors move in and out of the imperial precincts and hold themselves to strict discipline—they outshine other officials a hundredfold in probity.

sentences.zh: 按劾回庸，糾擿隱欺，比他吏相十也。

translations.literal: In investigating and impeaching the corrupt and exposing hidden deceit, they are ten times more effective than other officials.
translations.idiomatic: In investigating corruption and exposing hidden fraud they are ten times more effective than other officials.

sentences.zh: 陛下誠用臣言，妙擇能者委之，莫不盡力效死矣。

translations.literal: If Your Majesty truly adopts my words and selects the able to entrust with this charge, none will fail to exert their strength unto death.
translations.idiomatic: If Your Majesty adopts this plan and chooses capable men for the task, each will serve with his utmost loyalty.

sentences.zh: 」武後善之，下制析天下為二十道，擇堪使者。

translations.literal: Empress Wu approved it and issued an edict dividing the realm into twenty circuits and selecting suitable envoys.
translations.idiomatic: Empress Wu approved the proposal and ordered the realm divided into twenty circuits and suitable envoys chosen.

sentences.zh: 為眾議沮止。

translations.literal: It was blocked by general opinion.
translations.idiomatic: General opposition blocked the plan.

sentences.zh: 俄知天宮侍郎事，進麟臺少監、同鳳閣鸞臺平章事。

translations.literal: Soon he was made acting Vice Director of the Heavenly Palace and promoted to Vice Director of the Unicorn Terrace and Associate Grand Councilor of the Phoenix and Unicorn Pavilions.
translations.idiomatic: He soon served as acting Vice Director of the Heavenly Palace, then rose to Vice Director of the Unicorn Terrace and Associate Grand Councilor of the Phoenix and Unicorn Pavilions.

sentences.zh: 遷鸞臺侍郎。

translations.literal: He was transferred to Vice Director of the Phoenix Terrace.
translations.idiomatic: He was promoted to Vice Director of the Phoenix Terrace.

sentences.zh: 會張錫輔政，嶠，其出也，罷為成均祭酒。

translations.literal: When Zhang Xi entered the government, Qiao, being of the same faction, was removed and made Rector of the Imperial University.
translations.idiomatic: When Zhang Xi joined the government, Qiao—being of his faction—was dismissed to the post of Rector of the Imperial University.

sentences.zh: 俄檢校文昌左丞，留守東都。

translations.literal: Soon he was made acting Left Vice Director of the Palace of Literary Brilliance and left to guard the Eastern Capital.
translations.idiomatic: He was soon made acting Left Vice Director of the Palace of Literary Brilliance and appointed to guard the Eastern Capital.

sentences.zh: 長安三年，以本官復為平章事，知納言。

translations.literal: In the third year of Chang'an he resumed his former rank as Associate Grand Councilor and was made Director of the Palace Secretariat.
translations.idiomatic: In the third year of the Chang'an era he again became Associate Grand Councilor in his former capacity and was made Director of the Palace Secretariat.

sentences.zh: 遷內史，嶠辭劇，復為成均祭酒、平章事。

translations.literal: He was promoted to Grand Secretary; Qiao declined the heavy duties and was again made Rector of the Imperial University and Associate Grand Councilor.
translations.idiomatic: He was promoted to Grand Secretary, but Qiao declined the onerous post and returned to the posts of Rector of the Imperial University and Associate Grand Councilor.

sentences.zh: 武後將建大像於白司馬阪，嶠諫：「造像雖俾浮屠輸錢，然非州縣承辦不能濟，是名雖不稅而實稅之。

translations.literal: When Empress Wu was about to erect a great image at Baisima Slope, Qiao remonstrated: "Though image-making lets monks contribute money, it cannot be accomplished without prefectures and counties undertaking the work—in name there is no tax, but in fact there is taxation."
translations.idiomatic: When Empress Wu planned a great Buddha image at Baisima Slope, Qiao remonstrated: "Although the project is funded by Buddhist donations, prefectures and counties must carry it out—it is taxation in all but name."

sentences.zh: 臣計天下編戶，貧弱者眾，有賣舍、帖田供王役者。

translations.literal: Your servant reckons that among registered households under Heaven the poor and weak are many; some sell their houses or pawn their fields to supply imperial labor.
translations.idiomatic: I reckon that among registered households nationwide the poor are many—some sell their homes or pawn their fields to meet imperial levies.

sentences.zh: 今造像錢積十七萬緡，若頒之窮人，家給千錢，則紓十七萬戶饑寒之苦，德無窮矣。

translations.literal: The funds for the image now total one hundred seventy thousand strings; if distributed to the destitute, a thousand cash per household would relieve one hundred seventy thousand households of hunger and cold—virtue without end.
translations.idiomatic: The image fund now totals one hundred seventy thousand strings of cash; distributed to the destitute at a thousand cash per household, it would ease hunger and cold for one hundred seventy thousand families—an inexhaustible act of grace.

sentences.zh: 」不納。

translations.literal: The advice was not accepted.
translations.idiomatic: She did not accept the advice.

sentences.zh: 張易之敗，坐附會貶豫州刺史，未行，改通州。

translations.literal: When Zhang Yizhi fell, Qiao was punished for association and demoted to prefect of Yu Prefecture; before he departed he was changed to Tong Prefecture.
translations.idiomatic: After Zhang Yizhi's fall, Qiao was demoted to prefect of Yu for having sided with him; before he took up the post he was reassigned to Tong Prefecture.

sentences.zh: 數月，以吏部侍郎召，俄遷尚書。

translations.literal: After several months he was summoned as Vice Director of the Ministry of Personnel and soon promoted to Minister.
translations.idiomatic: Within months he was recalled as Vice Director of the Ministry of Personnel and soon promoted to Minister.

sentences.zh: 神龍二年，代韋安石為中書令。

translations.literal: In the second year of Shenlong he replaced Wei Anshi as Director of the Secretariat.
translations.idiomatic: In the second year of Shenlong he succeeded Wei Anshi as Director of the Secretariat.

sentences.zh: 嶠在吏部時，陰欲藉時望復宰相，乃奏置員外官數千。

translations.literal: While Qiao was in the Ministry of Personnel he secretly wished to use contemporary esteem to return to the chancellorship and memorialized to create several thousand supernumerary offices.
translations.idiomatic: While at the Ministry of Personnel, Qiao secretly hoped to win popular favor and regain the chancellorship; he memorialized to create several thousand supernumerary posts.

sentences.zh: 既吏眾猥，府庫虛耗，乃上書歸咎於時，因蓋向非，曰：

translations.literal: When officials became numerous and the treasury was drained, he submitted a memorial blaming the times and covering his former error, saying:
translations.idiomatic: When the bureaucracy swelled and the treasury was drained, he submitted a memorial blaming the times and masking his earlier mistake. He wrote:

sentences.zh: 元首之尊，居有重門擊柝之衛，出有清警戒道之禁，所以備非常，息異望，誠不可易舉動，慢防閑也。

translations.literal: The sovereign's dignity: at rest he has double gates and night-watch clappers for guard; abroad he has clear warnings and road clearance—this is to prepare against the unexpected and quiet irregular hopes. Truly one must not lightly move about or slacken precautions.
translations.idiomatic: The sovereign's dignity demands double gates and night watches at home, clear warnings and cleared roads abroad—all to guard against the unexpected and quell dangerous expectations. Your Majesty must not move lightly or relax these precautions.

sentences.zh: 陛下厭崇邃，輕尊嚴，微服潛遊，閱廛過市，行路私議，朝廷驚懼，如禍產意外，縱不自惜，奈宗廟蒼生何？

translations.literal: Your Majesty tires of lofty seclusion and treats dignity lightly, traveling in disguise and passing through markets and wards; travelers whisper privately, the court is alarmed and fearful as if disaster arose by surprise—even if you do not spare yourself, what of the ancestral temples and the common people?
translations.idiomatic: Your Majesty has grown weary of palace seclusion and treats your dignity lightly, traveling incognito through markets and lanes. Travelers whisper; the court trembles as if disaster might strike at any moment. Even if you care nothing for yourself, what of the ancestral temples and the people?

sentences.zh: 又分職建官，不可以濫。

translations.literal: Moreover in dividing duties and establishing offices, one must not be excessive.
translations.idiomatic: Moreover, offices must not be multiplied without need.

sentences.zh: 傳曰：「官不必備，惟其人。

translations.literal: The tradition says: "Offices need not all be filled—only the right men."
translations.idiomatic: The tradition says, "Offices need not all be filled—only the right men matter."

sentences.zh: 」自帝室中興，以不慎爵賞為惠，冒級躐階，朝升夕改，正闕不給，加以員外。

translations.literal: Since the imperial house's restoration, ranks and rewards have been dispensed without care as a favor; men leap grades and steps, promoted in the morning and changed at evening; regular posts cannot be supplied, and supernumeraries are added.
translations.idiomatic: Since the dynasty's restoration, ranks and rewards have been handed out carelessly as favors; men leap grades overnight; regular posts cannot be filled, and supernumeraries are piled on top.

sentences.zh: 內則府庫為殫，外則黎庶蒙害，非求賢助治之道也。

translations.literal: Within, the treasury is exhausted; without, the people suffer harm—this is not the way to seek the worthy and aid governance.
translations.idiomatic: Within, the treasury is drained; without, the people suffer—this is not how to seek talent and aid governance.

sentences.zh: 願愛晙班榮，息匪服之議。

translations.literal: I wish that honors and ranks be cherished and distributed with care, and talk of improper appointments cease.
translations.idiomatic: I ask that honors be granted with restraint and improper appointments cease.

sentences.zh: 今文武六十以上，而天造含容，皆矜恤之。

translations.literal: Now civil and military officials over sixty—the Heaven-made ruler is tolerant and pities them all.
translations.idiomatic: Civil and military officials over sixty are shown Heaven's mercy and treated with compassion.

sentences.zh: 老病者已解還授，員外者既遣復留。

translations.literal: The old and ill have been released and their posts reassigned, yet supernumeraries who were dismissed are kept again.
translations.idiomatic: The old and ill have been released and their posts reassigned, yet supernumeraries dismissed are kept on again.

sentences.zh: 恐非所以消敝救時也。

translations.literal: I fear this is not the way to relieve exhaustion and rescue the times.
translations.idiomatic: This is hardly the way to relieve strain and rescue the times.

sentences.zh: 請敕有司料其可用進，不可用退。

translations.literal: I ask that the authorities be ordered to assess who may be advanced and who should be removed.
translations.idiomatic: I ask that the authorities assess who may serve and who should be dismissed.

sentences.zh: 又遠方夷人不堪治事，國家向務撫納而官之，非立功酋長，類糜俸祿。

translations.literal: Moreover distant barbarians cannot manage affairs; the state has long sought to pacify and enroll them in office—those who are not chieftains who rendered merit mostly waste salaries.
translations.idiomatic: Distant tribesmen cannot govern; the state has long enrolled them in office for pacification—yet chieftains without merit mostly waste salaries.

sentences.zh: 願商度非要者，一切放還。

translations.literal: I wish that after deliberation those not needed be entirely sent home.
translations.idiomatic: I ask that after review all who are not needed be sent home.

sentences.zh: 又《易》稱：「何以守位曰仁，何以聚人曰財。

translations.literal: Moreover the Changes says: "By what does one keep one's position? By benevolence. By what does one gather people? By wealth."
translations.idiomatic: The Book of Changes says, "By what does one keep one's throne? By benevolence. By what does one gather the people? By wealth."

sentences.zh: 」今百姓乏窶，不安居處，不可以守位。

translations.literal: Now the common people are destitute and poor, without secure dwellings—they cannot keep the throne.
translations.idiomatic: Today the people are destitute and without secure homes—your throne cannot be held on such ground.

sentences.zh: 倉儲蕩耗，財力傾殫，不足以聚人。

translations.literal: Granaries are emptied and financial strength exhausted—there is not enough to gather people.
translations.idiomatic: Granaries are empty and the treasury exhausted—there is not enough wealth to hold the people together.

sentences.zh: 山東病水潦，江左困輸轉。

translations.literal: East of the mountains suffers from floods; south of the Yangtze is strained by transport levies.
translations.idiomatic: East of the mountains suffers floods; the lower Yangtze region is crushed by transport levies.

sentences.zh: 國匱於上，人窮於下。

translations.literal: The state is depleted above and the people impoverished below.
translations.idiomatic: The state is depleted above and the people impoverished below.

sentences.zh: 如令邊埸少曌，恐逋亡遂多，盜賊群行，何財召募？

translations.literal: If the frontier is now slightly quiet, I fear fugitives will multiply and bandits roam in groups—what wealth is there to recruit troops?
translations.idiomatic: If the frontier grows quiet for a time, fugitives will multiply and bandits roam in bands—what funds remain to raise troops?

sentences.zh: 何眾閑遏乎？

translations.literal: How can the masses be restrained in idleness?
translations.idiomatic: How can disorder among the people be checked?

sentences.zh: 又崇作寺觀，功費浩廣。

translations.literal: Moreover temples and monasteries are lavishly built, labor and expense vast.
translations.idiomatic: Moreover temples and monasteries are built on a lavish scale at enormous cost.

sentences.zh: 今山東歲饑，糟糠不厭。

translations.literal: Now east of the mountains suffers yearly famine; chaff and husks are not disdained.
translations.idiomatic: East of the mountains now suffers yearly famine; people are glad even for chaff and husks.

sentences.zh: 而投艱厄之會，收庸、調之半，用籲嗟之物，以榮土木，恐怨結三靈，謗蒙四海。

translations.literal: Yet in this time of hardship half of corvée and tax levies are taken, using what draws sighs to glorify timber and earth—I fear resentment binds the three spirits and slander covers the four seas.
translations.idiomatic: Yet in this time of hardship half of corvée and tax levies are taken from groaning households to glorify timber and stone—I fear resentment will reach Heaven and slander will spread across the realm.

sentences.zh: 又比緣征戍，巧詐百情，破役隱身，規脫租賦。

translations.literal: Moreover because of recent campaigns and garrison duty, cunning fraud takes a hundred forms—breaking labor service to hide oneself and scheming to escape taxes and levies.
translations.idiomatic: Recent campaigns and garrison duty have bred every kind of fraud—men evade labor service and scheme to escape taxes and levies.

sentences.zh: 今道人私度者幾數十萬，其中高戶多丁，黠商大賈，詭作臺符，羼名偽度。

translations.literal: Now those privately ordained as Daoist priests number nearly several hundred thousand; among them wealthy households with many sons, shrewd merchants and great traders forge court tallies and insert names for false ordination.
translations.idiomatic: Nearly several hundred thousand men have been privately ordained as Daoist priests—including wealthy households with many sons and shrewd merchants who forge court documents and take false ordination.

sentences.zh: 且國計軍防，並仰丁口，今丁皆出家，兵悉入道，征行租賦，何以備之？

translations.literal: Moreover state planning and military defense both rely on adult males; now adult males all leave home for the clergy and soldiers all enter the Way—how are campaigns, levies, and taxes to be supplied?
translations.idiomatic: State revenue and military defense both depend on adult males; now men enter the clergy and soldiers take religious vows—how are campaigns and taxes to be met?

sentences.zh: 又重賂貴近，補府若史，移沒籍產，以州縣甲等更為下戶。

translations.literal: Moreover by heavy bribes to the powerful near the throne men buy posts as prefectural clerks; registered property is transferred and confiscated, and their prefectural and county grades are changed to lower households.
translations.idiomatic: Heavy bribes to court favorites buy prefectural clerkships; registered property is transferred and confiscated, and household grades are lowered to escape tax.

sentences.zh: 當道城鎮，至無捉驛者，役逮小弱，即破其家。

translations.literal: In towns along the main routes there are sometimes none left to man relay stations; when corvée reaches the small and weak, their families are ruined at once.
translations.idiomatic: In towns along the main routes there are sometimes no men left to staff relay stations; when corvée falls on the weak, families are ruined overnight.

sentences.zh: 願許十道使訪察括取，使奸猾不得而隱。

translations.literal: I wish that envoys of the ten circuits be permitted to investigate and register them, so that the cunning cannot hide.
translations.idiomatic: I ask that envoys of the ten circuits investigate and register offenders so the cunning cannot hide.

sentences.zh: 又太常樂戶已多，復求訪散樂，獨持大鼓者已二萬員，願量留之，余勒還籍，以杜妄費。

translations.literal: Moreover the Court of Imperial Sacrifices' musician households are already many, yet scattered musicians are again sought; those who hold great drums alone number twenty thousand. I wish that a measured number be kept and the rest compelled to return to registration, to stop wasteful spending.
translations.idiomatic: The Court of Imperial Sacrifices already has too many musician households, yet more scattered musicians are sought—drummers alone number twenty thousand. I ask that only what is needed be kept and the rest returned to registration to stop waste.

sentences.zh: 中宗以嶠身宰相，乃自陳失政，丐罷官，無所嫁非，手詔詰讓。

translations.literal: Emperor Zhongzong, since Qiao himself was chancellor, took his self-accusation of misgovernment and plea to resign as blaming others without basis, and issued a personal edict rebuking him.
translations.idiomatic: Emperor Zhongzong, noting that Qiao himself was chancellor, saw his confession of misgovernment and plea to resign as blaming others without cause and issued a personal edict of rebuke.

sentences.zh: 嶠惶恐，復視事。

translations.literal: Qiao was fearful and resumed his duties.
translations.idiomatic: Qiao was alarmed and resumed his duties.

sentences.zh: 三年，加修文館大學士，封趙國公，以特進同中書門下三品。

translations.literal: In the third year he was made Grand Academician of the Hall for Cultivating Literature, enfeoffed as Duke of Zhao, and made Special Advancement with the rank of Third Grade, equal to the Secretariat.
translations.idiomatic: In the third year he was made Grand Academician of the Hall for Cultivating Literature, enfeoffed as Duke of Zhao, and granted Special Advancement with Third Grade rank equal to the Secretariat.

sentences.zh: 睿宗立，罷政事，下除懷州刺史，致仕。

translations.literal: When Emperor Ruizong ascended, Qiao was removed from government affairs, demoted to prefect of Huai Prefecture, and retired.
translations.idiomatic: When Emperor Ruizong ascended, Qiao left government, was demoted to prefect of Huai, and retired.

sentences.zh: 初，中宗崩，嶠嘗密請相王諸子不宜留京師。

translations.literal: Earlier, when Emperor Zhongzong died, Qiao had secretly memorialized that the Prince of Xiang's sons ought not remain in the capital.
translations.idiomatic: Earlier, when Emperor Zhongzong died, Qiao had secretly urged that the Prince of Xiang's sons should not remain in the capital.

sentences.zh: 及玄宗嗣位，獲其表宮中，或請誅之。

translations.literal: When Emperor Xuanzong succeeded, the memorial was found in the palace and some asked that he be executed.
translations.idiomatic: When Emperor Xuanzong succeeded, the memorial was found in the palace and some urged his execution.

sentences.zh: 張說曰：「嶠誠懵逆順，然為當時謀，吠非其主，不可追罪。

translations.literal: Zhang Yue said: "Qiao was indeed confused about what accords and what opposes, yet he acted as counsel for his time; a dog barks not at its master—his offense cannot be pursued."
translations.idiomatic: Zhang Yue said, "Qiao was indeed confused about loyalty, yet he acted as counsel for his time—a dog barks at strangers, not at its master; his offense cannot be punished retroactively."

sentences.zh: 」天子亦顧數更赦，遂免，貶滁州別駕，聽隨子虔州刺史暢之官。

translations.literal: The Son of Heaven also considered the many amnesties and pardoned him, demoting him to Vice Prefect of Chu and permitting him to follow his son Chang, prefect of Qian, to his post.
translations.idiomatic: The emperor also weighed the many amnesties and spared him, demoting him to Vice Prefect of Chu with permission to accompany his son Chang, prefect of Qian, to his post.

sentences.zh: 改廬州別駕，卒，年七十。

translations.literal: He was changed to Vice Prefect of Lu and died, aged seventy.
translations.idiomatic: He was reassigned to Vice Prefect of Lu and died at seventy.

sentences.zh: 嶠富才思，有所屬綴，人多傳諷。

translations.literal: Qiao was rich in literary talent; whenever he composed something, many transmitted and recited it.
translations.idiomatic: Qiao was richly gifted in letters; whatever he wrote was widely copied and recited.

sentences.zh: 武後時，汜水獲瑞石，嶠為御史，上《皇符》一篇，為世譏薄。

translations.literal: In Empress Wu's time a propitious stone was found at Sishui; as censor Qiao submitted a piece entitled "Imperial Talisman," which the age scorned.
translations.idiomatic: Under Empress Wu, when a propitious stone was found at Sishui, Qiao as censor submitted an essay entitled "Imperial Talisman," which the age scorned.

sentences.zh: 然其仕前與王勃、楊盈川接，中與崔融、蘇味道齊名，晚諸人沒，而為文章宿老，一時學者取法焉。

translations.literal: Yet in his early career he associated with Wang Bo and Yang Yingchuan; in mid-career he was famed equally with Cui Rong and Su Weidao; in late years, when the others had died, he became the senior master of letters, and scholars of the time took him as their model.
translations.idiomatic: In early career he moved in the circle of Wang Bo and Yang Yingchuan; in mid-career he ranked with Cui Rong and Su Weidao; in later years, after the others had died, he became the elder master of letters whom scholars of the age took as their model.

sentences.zh: 蕭至忠，沂州丞人。

translations.literal: Xiao Zhizhong was a man of Cheng in Yi Prefecture.
translations.idiomatic: Xiao Zhizhong was a native of Cheng in Yi Prefecture.

sentences.zh: 祖德言，為秘書少監。

translations.literal: His grandfather Deyan was Vice Director of the Secretariat.
translations.idiomatic: His grandfather Deyan served as Vice Director of the Secretariat.

sentences.zh: 至忠少與友期諸路，會雨雪，人引避，至忠曰：「寧有與人期可以失信？

translations.literal: Zhizhong in youth made an appointment with a friend at a crossroads; when snow and rain came, people urged him to take shelter. Zhizhong said: "Can one make an appointment with another and break faith?"
translations.idiomatic: As a youth Zhizhong arranged to meet a friend at a crossroads; when snow and rain came, others urged him to take shelter. He said, "How can one keep an appointment and break faith?"

sentences.zh: 」卒友至乃去，眾嘆服。

translations.literal: Only when his friend arrived did he leave; the crowd sighed in admiration.
translations.idiomatic: He left only after his friend arrived; onlookers marveled.

sentences.zh: 仕為伊闕、洛陽尉。

translations.literal: In office he served as magistrate of Yique and Luoyang.
translations.idiomatic: He served as magistrate of Yique and Luoyang.

sentences.zh: 遷監察御史，劾奏鳳閣侍郎蘇味道贓貪，超拜吏部員外郎。

translations.literal: He was promoted to investigating censor, impeached Vice Director Su Weidao of the Phoenix Pavilion for corruption, and was specially promoted to Vice Director in the Ministry of Personnel.
translations.idiomatic: Promoted to investigating censor, he impeached Vice Director Su Weidao of the Phoenix Pavilion for corruption and was specially promoted to Vice Director in the Ministry of Personnel.

sentences.zh: 至忠長擊斷，譽聞當時。

translations.literal: Zhizhong excelled in decisive judgment; his reputation was known in his time.
translations.idiomatic: Zhizhong was famed for decisive judgment and won renown in his day.

sentences.zh: 中宗神龍初，為御史中丞。

translations.literal: In the early Shenlong era of Emperor Zhongzong he became Vice Censor-in-Chief.
translations.idiomatic: In the early Shenlong era under Emperor Zhongzong he became Vice Censor-in-Chief.

sentences.zh: 始，至忠為御史，而李承嘉為大夫，嘗讓諸御史曰：「彈事有不咨大夫，可乎？

translations.literal: Earlier, when Zhizhong was a censor and Li Chengjia was chief censor, Li once rebuked the censors, saying: "In impeachment matters, is it permissible not to consult the chief censor?"
translations.idiomatic: Earlier, when Zhizhong was a censor and Li Chengjia was chief censor, Li once rebuked the censors: "In impeachment matters, is it permissible not to consult the chief censor?"

sentences.zh: 」眾不敢對，至忠獨曰：「故事，臺無長官。

translations.literal: None dared reply; Zhizhong alone said: "By precedent the Censorate has no chief officer."
translations.idiomatic: None dared reply; Zhizhong alone said, "By precedent the Censorate has no chief officer."

sentences.zh: 御史，天子耳目也，其所請奏當專達，若大夫許而後論，即劾大夫者，又誰白哉？

translations.literal: Censors are the Son of Heaven's eyes and ears; what they memorialize should reach him directly. If the chief censor must approve before discussion, then who will report the chief censor when he is impeached?
translations.idiomatic: Censors are the emperor's eyes and ears; their memorials should reach him directly. If the chief censor must approve first, who will report the chief censor when he is impeached?

sentences.zh: 」承嘉慚。

translations.literal: Chengjia was ashamed.
translations.idiomatic: Chengjia was ashamed.

sentences.zh: 至是，承嘉為戶部尚書，至忠劾祝欽明、竇希玠與承嘉等罪，百寮震悚。

translations.literal: By this time Chengjia was Minister of Revenue; Zhizhong impeached Zhu Qinming, Dou Xijie, and Chengjia and others for crimes, and the hundred officials trembled in awe.
translations.idiomatic: By then Chengjia was Minister of Revenue; Zhizhong impeached Zhu Qinming, Dou Xijie, Chengjia, and others for crimes, and the entire bureaucracy trembled.

sentences.zh: 遷吏部侍郎，猶兼中丞。

translations.literal: He was promoted to Vice Director of the Ministry of Personnel, still also serving as Vice Censor-in-Chief.
translations.idiomatic: He was promoted to Vice Director of the Ministry of Personnel while retaining the post of Vice Censor-in-Chief.

sentences.zh: 節湣太子以兵誅武三思而敗，宗楚客等諗侍御史冉祖雍上變，言相王與太子謀。

translations.literal: When Crown Prince Jiemin used troops to kill Wu Sansi and failed, Zong Chuke and others prompted Investigating Censor Ran Zuyong to submit an accusation, saying the Prince of Xiang and the crown prince had plotted together.
translations.idiomatic: When Crown Prince Jiemin raised troops to kill Wu Sansi and failed, Zong Chuke and others urged Investigating Censor Ran Zuyong to report a plot between the Prince of Xiang and the crown prince.

sentences.zh: 帝欲按之，至忠泣曰：「往者，天後欲以相王為太子，而王不食累日，獨請迎陛下，其讓德天下莫不聞。

translations.literal: The emperor wished to investigate; Zhizhong wept and said: "In the past Empress Tian wanted to make the Prince of Xiang crown prince, but the prince would not eat for days and alone asked to welcome Your Majesty back—his virtue of yielding was heard by all under Heaven."
translations.idiomatic: The emperor wished to investigate; Zhizhong wept and said, "In the past Empress Wu wanted to make the Prince of Xiang crown prince, but he fasted for days and alone asked to welcome Your Majesty back—his yielding virtue was known throughout the realm."

sentences.zh: 陛下貴為天子，不能容一弟，受人羅織耶？

translations.literal: Your Majesty is exalted as Son of Heaven yet cannot tolerate one younger brother—will you accept others' frame-ups?
translations.idiomatic: Your Majesty is Son of Heaven yet cannot tolerate one younger brother—will you accept others' fabrications?

sentences.zh: 竊為陛下不取。

translations.literal: I secretly deem it unworthy of Your Majesty.
translations.idiomatic: I cannot believe this is worthy of Your Majesty.

sentences.zh: 」帝納其言，止。

translations.literal: The emperor accepted his words and stopped.
translations.idiomatic: The emperor accepted his counsel and dropped the matter.

sentences.zh: 尋授中書侍郎、同中書門下平章事。

translations.literal: Soon he was appointed Vice Director of the Secretariat and Associate Director of the Secretariat.
translations.idiomatic: He was soon made Vice Director of the Secretariat and Associate Grand Councilor.

sentences.zh: 上疏陳時政曰：

translations.literal: He submitted a memorial setting forth current affairs, saying:
translations.idiomatic: He submitted a memorial on current affairs, saying:

sentences.zh: 求治之道，首於用賢。

translations.literal: The way to seek good governance begins with employing the worthy.
translations.idiomatic: The path to good governance begins with employing worthy men.

sentences.zh: 茍非其才則官曠，官曠則事廢，事廢則人殘，歷代所以陵遲者此也。

translations.literal: If men lack capacity, offices are empty; if offices are empty, affairs are abandoned; if affairs are abandoned, the people are harmed—this is why dynasties decline through the ages.
translations.idiomatic: If men lack talent, offices go unfilled; unfilled offices mean abandoned affairs; abandoned affairs ruin the people—this is how dynasties have declined through the ages.

sentences.zh: 今授職用人，多因貴要為粉飾，上下相蒙，茍得為是。

translations.literal: Now in appointing offices and employing men, many are embellished through powerful patrons; superiors and subordinates deceive one another, and mere acquiescence passes for right.
translations.idiomatic: Today appointments are often padded through powerful patrons; superiors and subordinates deceive one another, and mere acquiescence passes for right conduct.

sentences.zh: 夫官爵，公器也；

translations.literal: Office and rank are public instruments;
translations.idiomatic: Office and rank are instruments of the state;

sentences.zh: 恩幸，私惠也。

translations.literal: favor and grace are private bounty.
translations.idiomatic: favor and grace are private bounty.

sentences.zh: 王者正可金帛富之，梁肉食之，以存私澤也。

translations.literal: The king may rightly enrich favorites with gold and silk and feed them with fine grain and meat to preserve private favor.
translations.idiomatic: A ruler may rightly enrich favorites with gold and silk and feed them with fine fare to show private favor.

sentences.zh: 若公器而私用之，則公義不行而勞人解體，私謁開而正言塞。

translations.literal: If public instruments are used for private ends, public justice cannot prevail and the laboring people lose heart; private petitions open while upright speech is blocked.
translations.idiomatic: If public office is used for private ends, public justice fails and the people lose heart; private petitions flourish while honest counsel is silenced.

sentences.zh: 日朘月削，卒見雕弊。

translations.literal: Day by day it is whittled away, month by month reduced, until at last ruin appears.
translations.idiomatic: Day by day the state is whittled away until ruin appears.

sentences.zh: 今列位已廣，冗員復倍。

translations.literal: Now established posts are already broad, and supernumeraries have doubled again.
translations.idiomatic: Established posts are already numerous, and supernumeraries have doubled again.

sentences.zh: 陛下降不呰之澤，近戚有無涯之請，臺閣之內，朱紫充滿，官秩益輕，恩賞彌數。

translations.literal: Your Majesty bestows boundless grace; close kin have endless requests; within the ministries crimson and purple fill the halls, ranks grow ever lighter, and favors and rewards multiply.
translations.idiomatic: Your Majesty bestows boundless grace; close kin make endless requests; the ministries are crowded with crimson and purple robes, ranks grow ever cheaper, and favors multiply without end.

sentences.zh: 才者不用，用者不才，故人不效力，官匪其人，欲求治固難矣。

translations.literal: The talented are not used; those used lack talent—thus men do not exert themselves, offices do not match their holders, and to seek good governance is indeed hard.
translations.idiomatic: The talented go unused; the appointed lack talent—men do not exert themselves, offices do not match their holders, and good governance is indeed hard to achieve.

sentences.zh: 又宰相要官子弟，多居美爵，並罕才藝，而更相諉托。

translations.literal: Moreover the sons of chancellors and important officials mostly hold fine ranks, all rarely possessing talent or skill, yet recommending one another in turn.
translations.idiomatic: Moreover the sons of chancellors and high officials mostly hold fine ranks though they rarely possess talent, yet they recommend one another in turn.

sentences.zh: 《詩》云：「私人之子，百寮是試。

translations.literal: The Odes says: "Sons of private families—the hundred officers are tried on them."
translations.idiomatic: The Book of Odes says, "Sons of private families—the hundred officers are tried on them."

sentences.zh: 或以其酒，不以其漿，鞙鞙佩遂，不以其長。

translations.literal: "Some take their wine, not their brew; tinkling pendants hang at the girdle, not by their length."
translations.idiomatic: "Some take their wine, not their brew; tinkling pendants hang at the girdle, not by their length."

sentences.zh: 」此言王政不平而眾官廢職，私家子列試榮班，徒長其佩爾。

translations.literal: This speaks of royal government not being level and the hundred officers abandoning duty—private sons are ranked in trial for honored posts, merely lengthening their pendants.
translations.idiomatic: This means that when royal government is unjust, officials abandon their duties—private sons are placed in honored ranks merely to lengthen their pendants.

sentences.zh: 臣願陛下愛惜爵賞，官無虛授，進大雅以樞近，退小人於閑左，使政令惟一，私不害公，則天下幸甚。

translations.literal: Your servant wishes Your Majesty to cherish ranks and rewards, grant no empty offices, advance great talents to the center, retire petty men to the margins, make government orders single and private interest not harm the public—then all under Heaven would be greatly blessed.
translations.idiomatic: I ask Your Majesty to cherish ranks and rewards, grant no empty offices, advance great talents to the center, retire petty men to the margins, unify government orders, and keep private interest from harming the public—then the realm would be greatly blessed.

sentences.zh: 且貞觀故事，宰相子弟多居外職，非直抑強宗，亦以擇賢才爾。

translations.literal: Moreover by Zhenguan precedent chancellors' sons mostly held outer posts—not only to restrain powerful clans but also to select worthy talent.
translations.idiomatic: Under Zhenguan precedent chancellors' sons mostly held provincial posts—not only to restrain powerful clans but also to select worthy talent.

sentences.zh: 請自宰相及諸司長官子弟，並授外官，共寧百性，表裏相統。

translations.literal: I ask that from the chancellor and the sons of directors of all ministries onward, all be given outer offices, together bringing peace to the hundred surnames, inner and outer mutually coordinated.
translations.idiomatic: I ask that the sons of chancellors and ministry directors all be given provincial posts, bringing peace to the people and coordinating court and provinces.

sentences.zh: 帝不納。

translations.literal: The emperor did not accept it.
translations.idiomatic: The emperor did not accept the proposal.

sentences.zh: 俄為侍中、中書令。

translations.literal: Soon he became Palace Attendant and Director of the Secretariat.
translations.idiomatic: He soon became Palace Attendant and Director of the Secretariat.

sentences.zh: 時楚客懷奸植黨，而韋巨源、楊再思、李嶠務自安，無所弼正，至忠介其間，獨不詭隨，時望翕然歸重。

translations.literal: At that time Chuke harbored treachery and planted factions, while Wei Juyuan, Yang Zaisi, and Li Qiao sought only their own safety and offered no correction; Zhizhong stood among them alone not bending with the current, and contemporary esteem converged upon him.
translations.idiomatic: Chuke then harbored treachery and built factions, while Wei Juyuan, Yang Zaisi, and Li Qiao sought only their own safety and offered no correction; Zhizhong alone refused to bend with the current, and public esteem converged upon him.

sentences.zh: 帝亦曰：「宰相中，至忠最憐我。

translations.literal: The emperor also said: "Among the chancellors, Zhizhong pities me most."
translations.idiomatic: The emperor also said, "Among the chancellors, Zhizhong cares for me most."

sentences.zh: 」韋後嘗為其弟洵與至忠殤女冥婚。

translations.literal: Empress Wei once arranged a posthumous marriage between her brother Xun and Zhizhong's deceased daughter.
translations.idiomatic: Empress Wei once arranged a posthumous marriage between her brother Xun and Zhizhong's deceased daughter.

sentences.zh: 至忠又以女妻後舅崔從禮子無诐。

translations.literal: Zhizhong also gave a daughter in marriage to Wu Bi, son of the empress's uncle Cui Congli.
translations.idiomatic: Zhizhong also gave a daughter in marriage to Wu Bi, son of the empress's uncle Cui Congli.

sentences.zh: 兩家合禮，帝主蕭，後主崔，時謂「天子嫁女，皇后娶婦。」

translations.literal: When the two families united in ceremony, the emperor presided for the Xiao and the empress for the Cui; the age said, "The Son of Heaven marries out a daughter, the empress takes in a daughter-in-law."
translations.idiomatic: When the two families united in ceremony, the emperor presided for the Xiao side and the empress for the Cui; the age said, "The Son of Heaven marries out a daughter, the empress takes in a daughter-in-law."

sentences.zh: 至忠始在朝，有風望，容止閑敏，見推為名臣。

translations.literal: Zhizhong at first in court had reputation and bearing, deportment refined and quick, and was praised as a famed minister.
translations.idiomatic: Early in his career Zhizhong enjoyed reputation and bearing, refined and quick in deportment, and was praised as a famed minister.

sentences.zh: 外方直，糾擿不法，而內無守，觀時輕重而去就之。

translations.literal: Outwardly upright, he impeached what was unlawful, yet inwardly he had no constancy and weighed the times' shifts in going and staying.
translations.idiomatic: Outwardly upright, he impeached wrongdoing, yet inwardly he lacked constancy and shifted with the times.

sentences.zh: 始為御史，桓彥範等頗引重。

translations.literal: When he first became censor, Huan Yanfan and others greatly valued him.
translations.idiomatic: When he first became censor, Huan Yanfan and others greatly valued him.

sentences.zh: 五王失政，更因武三思得中丞，附安樂公主為宰相。

translations.literal: When the Five Princes lost power, he again through Wu Sansi obtained the vice censorate, attached himself to Princess Anle, and became chancellor.
translations.idiomatic: After the Five Princes fell, he again obtained the vice censorate through Wu Sansi, attached himself to Princess Anle, and became chancellor.

sentences.zh: 及韋氏敗，遽發韋洵壟，持其女柩歸。

translations.literal: When the Wei clan fell, he hastily opened Wei Xun's tomb and took his daughter's coffin home.
translations.idiomatic: When the Wei clan fell, he hastily opened Wei Xun's tomb and took his daughter's coffin home.

sentences.zh: 後依太平，復當國。

translations.literal: Later he relied on Princess Taiping and again held the government.
translations.idiomatic: Later he relied on Princess Taiping and again held power.

sentences.zh: 嘗出主第，遇宋璟，璟戲曰：「非所望於蕭傅。

translations.literal: Once leaving the princess's mansion he met Song Jing; Jing jested: "This is not what was hoped of Master Xiao."
translations.idiomatic: Once leaving the princess's mansion he met Song Jing, who jested, "This is not what was hoped of Master Xiao."

sentences.zh: 」至忠曰：「善乎，宋生之言。

translations.literal: Zhizhong said: "Well said, Master Song's words."
translations.idiomatic: Zhizhong said, "Well said, Master Song."

sentences.zh: 」然不能自返也。

translations.literal: Yet he could not turn back.
translations.idiomatic: Yet he could not turn back.

sentences.zh: 娣嫁蔣欽緒，欽緒每戒之，至忠不聽。

translations.literal: His younger sister married Jiang Qinxu; Qinxu often warned him, but Zhizhong would not listen.
translations.idiomatic: His younger sister married Jiang Qinxu, who often warned him, but Zhizhong would not listen.

sentences.zh: 嘆曰：「九世卿族，一舉而滅之，可哀也已！

translations.literal: He sighed: "A ministerial clan of nine generations, destroyed in one stroke—how lamentable!"
translations.idiomatic: He sighed, "A ministerial clan of nine generations, destroyed in one stroke—how lamentable!"

sentences.zh: 」不喜接賓客，以簡儉自高，故生平奉賜，無所遺施，及籍沒，珍寶不可計。

translations.literal: He did not like receiving guests and prided himself on simplicity and frugality, so in life his stipends and gifts were nowhere bestowed; yet when his property was confiscated, treasures were beyond counting.
translations.idiomatic: He disliked receiving guests and prided himself on frugality, so in life he gave away nothing from his stipends; yet when his property was confiscated, treasures were beyond counting.

sentences.zh: 然玄宗賢其為人，後得源乾曜，亟用之，謂高力士曰：「若知吾進乾曜遽乎？

translations.literal: Yet Emperor Xuanzong esteemed his character; later obtaining Yuan Qianyao, he quickly employed him and said to Gao Lishi: "Do you know how swiftly I advanced Qianyao?"
translations.idiomatic: Yet Emperor Xuanzong esteemed his character; later, when he obtained Yuan Qianyao, he quickly employed him and said to Gao Lishi, "Do you know how swiftly I advanced Qianyao?"

sentences.zh: 吾以其貌言似蕭至忠。

translations.literal: "I took his appearance and speech as resembling Xiao Zhizhong."
translations.idiomatic: "I took his appearance and manner as resembling Xiao Zhizhong."

sentences.zh: 」力士曰：「彼不嘗負陛下乎？

translations.literal: Lishi said: "Did he not once betray Your Majesty?"
translations.idiomatic: Lishi said, "Did he not once betray Your Majesty?"

sentences.zh: 」帝曰：「至忠誠國器，但晚謬爾，其始不謂之賢哉？」

translations.literal: The emperor said: "Zhizhong was truly an instrument of state, but erred late—was he not called worthy at the start?"
translations.idiomatic: The emperor said, "Zhizhong was truly a pillar of state, but erred in his later years—was he not called worthy at the start?"

sentences.zh: 弟元嘉，工部侍郎；

translations.literal: His younger brother Yuanjia was Vice Director of the Ministry of Works;
translations.idiomatic: His younger brother Yuanjia was Vice Director of the Ministry of Works;

sentences.zh: 廣微，工部員外郎。

translations.literal: Guangwei was Vice Director in the Ministry of Works.
translations.idiomatic: Guangwei was Vice Director in the Ministry of Works.

sentences.zh: 盧藏用，字子潛，幽州范陽人。

translations.literal: Lu Zangyong, styled Ziqian, was a man of Fanyang in You Prefecture.
translations.idiomatic: Lu Zangyong, courtesy name Ziqian, was a native of Fanyang in You Prefecture.

sentences.zh: 父敬，魏州長史，號才吏。

translations.literal: His father Jing was Long Secretary of Wei Prefecture and was called a talented official.
translations.idiomatic: His father Jing served as Long Secretary of Wei Prefecture and was known as a talented official.

sentences.zh: 藏用能屬文，舉進士，不得調。

translations.literal: Zangyong could compose literary pieces, passed the jinshi examination, but received no appointment.
translations.idiomatic: Zangyong could compose literary pieces, passed the jinshi examination, but received no appointment.

sentences.zh: 與兄徵明偕隱終南、少室二山，學練氣，為辟谷，登衡、廬，仿徉岷、峨。

translations.literal: With his elder brother Zhengming he retired together to the two mountains Zhongnan and Shaoshi, studied breath cultivation, practiced grain avoidance, climbed Heng and Lu, and wandered Min and Emei.
translations.idiomatic: With his elder brother Zhengming he retired to Zhongnan and Shaoshi mountains, practiced breath cultivation and grain avoidance, climbed Mount Heng and Mount Lu, and wandered Mount Min and Mount Emei.

sentences.zh: 與陳子昂、趙貞固友善。

translations.literal: He was friendly with Chen Zi'ang and Zhao Zhengu.
translations.idiomatic: He was close friends with Chen Zi'ang and Zhao Zhengu.

sentences.zh: 長安中，召授左拾遺。

translations.literal: In the Chang'an era he was summoned and appointed Left Reminder.
translations.idiomatic: During the Chang'an era he was summoned and appointed Left Reminder.

sentences.zh: 武後作興泰宮於萬安山，上疏諫曰：「陛下離宮別觀固多矣，又窮人力以事土木，臣恐議者以陛下為不愛人而奉己也。

translations.literal: When Empress Wu built the Xingtai Palace on Mount Wan'an, he submitted a remonstrance: "Your Majesty's detached palaces and separate pavilions are already many; again exhausting human labor for timber and earth—I fear critics will take Your Majesty as not loving the people but serving yourself."
translations.idiomatic: When Empress Wu built the Xingtai Palace on Mount Wan'an, he remonstrated: "Your Majesty already has many detached palaces; to exhaust human labor again on timber and earth—I fear critics will say you do not love the people but serve yourself."

sentences.zh: 且頃歲谷雖頗登，而百姓未有儲。

translations.literal: Moreover in recent years though grain has been fairly abundant, the common people have no stores.
translations.idiomatic: Moreover, though harvests have been fair in recent years, the people have no reserves.

sentences.zh: 陛下巡幸，訖靡休息，斤斧之役，歲月不空，不因此時施德布化，而又廣宮苑，臣恐下未易堪。

translations.literal: Your Majesty's tours and visits never cease to rest; axe and adze labor never leaves the months empty. If at such a time you do not spread virtue and disseminate transformation but instead expand palaces and parks, I fear those below will not easily bear it.
translations.idiomatic: Your tours never cease; timber work never leaves the year idle. If you do not spread virtue at such a time but instead expand palaces and parks, I fear the people cannot bear it.

sentences.zh: 今左右近臣，以諛意為忠，犯忤為患，至令陛下不知百姓失業，百姓亦不知左右傷陛下之仁也。

translations.literal: Now those near at hand take flattery for loyalty and offense for harm, until Your Majesty does not know the people's loss of livelihood and the people also do not know how those at hand wound Your Majesty's benevolence.
translations.idiomatic: Those near you take flattery for loyalty and offense for harm, until you do not know the people's loss of livelihood and the people do not know how your courtiers wound your benevolence.

sentences.zh: 忠臣不避誅震以納君於仁，明主不惡切詆以趨名於後。

translations.literal: Loyal ministers do not avoid punishment and awe to lead the ruler into benevolence; enlightened rulers do not hate sharp criticism to win fame after death.
translations.idiomatic: Loyal ministers do not shrink from punishment to lead the ruler toward benevolence; enlightened rulers do not hate sharp criticism to win lasting fame.

sentences.zh: 陛下誠能發明制，以勞人為辭，則天下必以為愛力而苦己也。

translations.literal: If Your Majesty truly can issue a clear edict taking labor on the people as its reason, all under Heaven will surely deem you as loving their strength yet suffering for yourself.
translations.idiomatic: If Your Majesty issues a clear edict citing the burden on the people, the realm will surely see you as loving their strength yet suffering for yourself.

sentences.zh: 不然，下臣此章，得與執事者共議。

translations.literal: Otherwise, this memorial of your low servant may be discussed together with those in charge.
translations.idiomatic: Otherwise, let this memorial of mine be discussed with those in charge.

sentences.zh: 」不從。

translations.literal: The advice was not followed.
translations.idiomatic: She did not follow the advice.

sentences.zh: 姚元崇持節靈武道，奏為管記。

translations.literal: Yao Yuanchong held credentials on the Lingwu circuit and memorialized to make him staff recorder.
translations.idiomatic: Yao Yuanchong, holding credentials on the Lingwu circuit, had him appointed staff recorder.

sentences.zh: 還應縣令舉，甲科，為濟陽令。

translations.literal: On return he responded to the magistrates' recommendation, passed in the top grade, and became magistrate of Jiyang.
translations.idiomatic: On return he responded to the magistrates' recommendation, passed in the top grade, and became magistrate of Jiyang.

sentences.zh: 神龍中，累擢中書舍人，數糾駁偽官。

translations.literal: In the Shenlong era he was repeatedly promoted to Secretariat Aide and several times impeached false officials.
translations.idiomatic: During the Shenlong era he rose to Secretariat Aide and repeatedly impeached false officials.

sentences.zh: 歷吏部、黃門侍郎、脩文館學士。

translations.literal: He served as Vice Director in the Ministries of Personnel and of the Palace Gate, and as Academician of the Hall for Cultivating Literature.
translations.idiomatic: He served as Vice Director in the Ministries of Personnel and of the Palace Gate, and as Academician of the Hall for Cultivating Literature.

sentences.zh: 坐親累，降工部侍郎。

translations.literal: Punished through kin association, he was demoted to Vice Director of the Ministry of Works.
translations.idiomatic: Implicated through kin association, he was demoted to Vice Director of the Ministry of Works.

sentences.zh: 進尚書右丞。

translations.literal: He was promoted to Right Vice Director of the Ministry of State.
translations.idiomatic: He was promoted to Right Vice Director of the Ministry of State.

sentences.zh: 附太平公主，主誅，玄宗欲捕斬藏用，顧未執政，意解，乃流新州。

translations.literal: He attached himself to Princess Taiping; when the princess was executed, Xuanzong wished to capture and execute Zangyong, but seeing he had not yet held government, his mind eased, and Zangyong was exiled to Xin Prefecture.
translations.idiomatic: He sided with Princess Taiping; when she was executed, Xuanzong wished to capture and execute Zangyong, but seeing he had not yet held power, relented and exiled him to Xin Prefecture.

sentences.zh: 或告謀反，推無狀，流州。

translations.literal: Someone reported rebellion; investigation found no grounds, and he was exiled within the prefecture.
translations.idiomatic: Someone reported rebellion; investigation found no grounds, and he was exiled within the prefecture.

sentences.zh: 會交趾叛，藏用有捍禦勞，改昭州司戶參軍，遷黔州長史，判都督事，卒於始興。

translations.literal: When Jiaozhi rebelled, Zangyong had merit in defense; he was changed to Registrar in Zha Prefecture, promoted to Long Secretary of Qian Prefecture and acting military commissioner, and died at Shixing.
translations.idiomatic: When Jiaozhi rebelled, Zangyong earned merit in defense; he was made Registrar in Zha Prefecture, promoted to Long Secretary of Qian Prefecture acting as military commissioner, and died at Shixing.

sentences.zh: 藏用善蓍龜九宮術，工草隸、大小篆、八分，善琴、弈，思精遠，士貴其多能。

translations.literal: Zangyong was skilled in milfoil, tortoise, and nine-palace arts, excelled in cursive, clerical, large and small seal, and eight-part scripts, was good at zither and go, his thought refined and far-reaching; scholars prized his many talents.
translations.idiomatic: Zangyong was skilled in divination and the nine-palace arts, excelled in cursive, clerical, seal, and eight-part scripts, played zither and go expertly, and thought with refined depth; scholars prized his many talents.

sentences.zh: 嘗以俗徇陰陽拘畏，乖至理，泥變通，有國者所不宜專。

translations.literal: He once held that custom's submission to yin-yang taboos and fears departs from supreme principle, clings to rigidity, and is what those who hold a state ought not specialize in.
translations.idiomatic: He held that popular submission to yin-yang taboos departs from supreme principle, clings to rigidity, and is what rulers ought not rely on exclusively.

sentences.zh: 謂：「天道從人者也。

translations.literal: He said: "The Way of Heaven follows the human."
translations.idiomatic: He said, "The Way of Heaven follows the human realm."

sentences.zh: 古為政者，刑獄不濫則人壽，賦斂省則人富，法令有常則邦寧，賞罰中則兵強。

translations.literal: Ancient rulers: if punishments and prisons were not excessive, people lived long; if levies were reduced, people grew rich; if laws and orders were constant, the state was tranquil; if rewards and punishments were balanced, troops were strong.
translations.idiomatic: Ancient rulers knew that if punishments were not excessive, people lived long; if levies were light, people grew rich; if laws were stable, the state was tranquil; if rewards and punishments were balanced, armies were strong.

sentences.zh: 禮者士所歸，賞者士所死，禮賞不倦，則士爭先，否者，雖揆時行罰，涓日出號，無成功矣。

translations.literal: Rites are what gentlemen return to; rewards are what gentlemen die for. If rites and rewards never weary, gentlemen vie to be first; otherwise, though one measures the times and imposes punishments, issuing orders day by day, there is no success.
translations.idiomatic: Rites are what gentlemen honor; rewards are what they die for. If rites and rewards never fail, gentlemen vie to serve; otherwise, though one times punishments and issues orders daily, nothing succeeds.

sentences.zh: 故任賢使能，不時日而利；

translations.literal: Thus employing the worthy and using the able brings benefit without regard to days;
translations.idiomatic: Thus employing the worthy brings benefit without regard to auspicious days;

sentences.zh: 明法審令，不卜筮而吉；

translations.literal: clarifying law and examining orders brings good fortune without divination;
translations.idiomatic: clarifying law and examining orders brings good fortune without divination;

sentences.zh: 養勞貴功，不禱祠而福。

translations.literal: nourishing toil and honoring merit brings blessing without prayer and sacrifice.
translations.idiomatic: nourishing toil and honoring merit brings blessing without prayer and sacrifice.

sentences.zh: 」乃為《析滯論》以暢其方，世謂「知言」。

translations.literal: He then wrote "Discourse on Dispelling Stagnation" to expound his method; the age called it "words that know."
translations.idiomatic: He then wrote "Discourse on Dispelling Stagnation" to expound his views; the age called it "words of insight."

sentences.zh: 子昂、貞固前死，藏用撫其孤有恩，人稱能終始交。

translations.literal: Zi'ang and Zhengu had died earlier; Zangyong nurtured their orphans with kindness, and men praised him for friendship maintained to the end.
translations.idiomatic: After Zi'ang and Zhengu died, Zangyong nurtured their orphans with kindness, and men praised him for friendship maintained to the end.

sentences.zh: 始隱山中時，有意當世，人目為「隨駕隱士」。

translations.literal: When he first hid in the mountains he had intent toward the age; men regarded him as a "hermit who follows the imperial carriage."
translations.idiomatic: When he first retired to the mountains he still aimed at public office; men called him a "hermit who follows the imperial carriage."

sentences.zh: 晚乃徇權利，務為驕縱，素節盡矣。

translations.literal: In later years he pursued power and profit, strove to be arrogant and unrestrained, and his former integrity was wholly gone.
translations.idiomatic: In later years he pursued power and profit, grew arrogant and unrestrained, and his former integrity was gone.

sentences.zh: 司馬承禎嘗召至闕下，將還山，藏用指終南曰：「此中大有嘉處。

translations.literal: Sima Chengzhen once summoned him to the palace; as he was about to return to the mountains, Zangyong pointed to Zhongnan and said: "Within this there are many fine places."
translations.idiomatic: Sima Chengzhen once summoned him to court; as he was about to return to the mountains, Zangyong pointed to Zhongnan and said, "There are many fine places here."

sentences.zh: 」承禎徐曰：「以仆視之，仕宦之捷徑耳。

translations.literal: Chengzhen said slowly: "As I see it, this is but a shortcut to office and rank."
translations.idiomatic: Chengzhen said slowly, "As I see it, this is but a shortcut to office and rank."

sentences.zh: 」藏用慚。

translations.literal: Zangyong was ashamed.
translations.idiomatic: Zangyong was ashamed.

sentences.zh: 無子。

translations.literal: He had no sons.
translations.idiomatic: He had no sons.

sentences.zh: 弟若虛，多才博物。

translations.literal: His younger brother Ruoxu was richly talented and broadly learned in things.
translations.idiomatic: His younger brother Ruoxu was richly talented and broadly learned.

sentences.zh: 隴西辛怡諫為職方，有獲異鼠者，豹首虎臆，大如拳。

translations.literal: Xin Yijian of Longxi was in the Bureau of Operations; someone obtained a strange rat with leopard head and tiger breast, large as a fist.
translations.idiomatic: Xin Yijian of Longxi served in the Bureau of Operations; someone obtained a strange rat with a leopard's head and tiger's breast, as large as a fist.

sentences.zh: 怡諫謂之鼮鼠而賦之。

translations.literal: Yijian called it a flying rat and composed a rhapsody on it.
translations.idiomatic: Yijian called it a flying rat and composed a rhapsody on it.

sentences.zh: 若虛曰：「非也，此許慎所謂鼨鼠，豹文而形小。

translations.literal: Ruoxu said: "Not so—this is what Xu Shen calls the patterned rat, leopard-marked and small in form."
translations.idiomatic: Ruoxu said, "Not so—this is what Xu Shen calls the patterned rat, leopard-marked and small in form."

sentences.zh: 」一坐驚服。

translations.literal: The whole company was startled and convinced.
translations.idiomatic: The whole company marveled.

sentences.zh: 終起居郎，集賢院學士。

translations.literal: He ended as Attendant of the Palace Secretariat and Academician of the Hall of Assembled Talents.
translations.idiomatic: He ended as Attendant of the Palace Secretariat and Academician of the Hall of Assembled Talents.

sentences.zh: 韋巨源，與安石同系，後周京兆尹總曾孫。

translations.literal: Wei Juyuan was of the same lineage as Anshi and great-great-grandson of Zong, Metropolitan Governor of the Later Zhou.
translations.idiomatic: Wei Juyuan was of the same lineage as Wei Anshi and great-great-grandson of Zong, Metropolitan Governor under the Later Zhou.

sentences.zh: 祖貞伯，襲鄖國公，入隋，改舒國。

translations.literal: His grandfather Zhenbo inherited the title Duke of Yun and entered Sui, where the fief was changed to Shu.
translations.idiomatic: His grandfather Zhenbo inherited the title Duke of Yun; under Sui the fief was changed to Shu.

sentences.zh: 巨源有吏幹，武後時累遷夏官侍郎、同鳳閣鸞臺平章事。

translations.literal: Juyuan had administrative talent; in Empress Wu's time he was repeatedly promoted to Vice Director of the Ministry of War and Associate Grand Councilor of the Phoenix and Unicorn Pavilions.
translations.idiomatic: Juyuan had administrative talent; under Empress Wu he rose to Vice Director of the Ministry of War and Associate Grand Councilor.

sentences.zh: 其治委碎無大體，句校省中遺隱，下符斂克不少蠲，雖收其利，然下所怨苦。

translations.literal: His governance was petty and lacked large design; he audited hidden omissions in the ministries and sent orders to collect and exact without much remission—though he gathered profit, those below resented and suffered.
translations.idiomatic: His governance was petty and lacked large design; he audited hidden omissions in the ministries and sent orders to collect levies with little remission—though he gathered revenue, those below resented and suffered.

sentences.zh: 坐李昭德累，貶鄜州刺史。

translations.literal: Punished through Li Zhaode's case, he was demoted to prefect of Fu Prefecture.
translations.idiomatic: Implicated in Li Zhaode's case, he was demoted to prefect of Fu Prefecture.

sentences.zh: 累拜地官尚書。

translations.literal: He was repeatedly promoted to Minister of Revenue.
translations.idiomatic: He was repeatedly promoted to Minister of Revenue.

sentences.zh: 神龍初，以吏部尚書同中書門下三品。

translations.literal: In early Shenlong he became Minister of Personnel with Third Grade rank equal to the Secretariat.
translations.idiomatic: In early Shenlong he became Minister of Personnel with Third Grade rank equal to the Secretariat.

sentences.zh: 時要官缺，執政以次用其親，巨源秉筆，當除十人，楊再思得其一，試問余授，皆諸宰相近屬。

translations.literal: At that time important offices were vacant; those in power used their kin in turn. Juyuan held the brush; ten men were to be appointed; Yang Zaisi got one. Asked about the rest, all were close kin of the various chancellors.
translations.idiomatic: Important offices were vacant; those in power appointed their kin in turn. Juyuan held the brush for ten appointments; Yang Zaisi got one. Asked about the rest, all were close kin of the chancellors.

sentences.zh: 再思喟然曰：「吾等誠負天下。

translations.literal: Zaisi sighed and said: "We truly fail all under Heaven."
translations.idiomatic: Zaisi sighed and said, "We truly fail the realm."

sentences.zh: 」巨源曰：「時當爾耳。

translations.literal: Juyuan said: "The times require no less."
translations.idiomatic: Juyuan said, "The times require no less."

sentences.zh: 」是時雖賢有德，終莫得進，士大夫莫不解體。

translations.literal: At that time though men were worthy and virtuous, in the end none could advance; scholar-officials all lost heart.
translations.idiomatic: Though worthy men existed, none could advance; scholar-officials lost heart.

sentences.zh: 會安石為中書令，避親罷政事。

translations.literal: When Anshi became Director of the Secretariat, Juyuan withdrew from government to avoid kin conflict.
translations.idiomatic: When Wei Anshi became Director of the Secretariat, Juyuan left government to avoid kin conflict.

sentences.zh: 尋遷侍中，舒國公。

translations.literal: Soon he was promoted to Palace Attendant and Duke of Shu.
translations.idiomatic: He was soon promoted to Palace Attendant and enfeoffed as Duke of Shu.

sentences.zh: 韋後與敘昆弟，附屬籍。

translations.literal: Empress Wei treated him as a sworn brother and enrolled him in the clan register.
translations.idiomatic: Empress Wei treated him as a sworn brother and enrolled him in the clan register.

sentences.zh: 武三思封戶在貝州，屬大水，刺史宋璟議免其租，巨源以為蠶桑可輸，繇是河朔人多流徙者。

translations.literal: Wu Sansi's fief households were in Bei Prefecture, which suffered great flood; Prefect Song Jing proposed remitting their rent. Juyuan held that silkworms and mulberry could still be delivered—hence many north of the Yellow River fled and migrated.
translations.idiomatic: Wu Sansi's fief households in Bei Prefecture suffered great flood; Prefect Song Jing proposed remitting their rent. Juyuan held that tribute could still be delivered—hence many north of the Yellow River fled.

sentences.zh: 景龍二年。

translations.literal: In the second year of Jinglong.
translations.idiomatic: In the second year of Jinglong.

sentences.zh: 韋後自言衣笥有五色雲，巨源倡其偽，勸中宗宣布天下，帝從其言，因是大赦。

translations.literal: Empress Wei said herself that five-colored clouds appeared in her wardrobe; Juyuan led the falsehood and urged Zhongzong to proclaim it to all under Heaven. The emperor followed his words and thereby issued a great amnesty.
translations.idiomatic: Empress Wei claimed five-colored clouds appeared in her wardrobe; Juyuan promoted the fraud and urged Zhongzong to proclaim it to the realm. The emperor complied and issued a great amnesty.

sentences.zh: 巨源見帝昏惑，乃與宗楚客、鄭愔、趙延禧等推處祥妖，陰導韋氏行武後故事。

translations.literal: Juyuan saw the emperor benighted and confused; with Zong Chuke, Zheng Yin, Zhao Yanxi, and others he interpreted omens and prodigies and secretly guided the Wei clan to follow Empress Wu's precedent.
translations.idiomatic: Seeing the emperor benighted, Juyuan with Zong Chuke, Zheng Yin, Zhao Yanxi, and others interpreted omens and secretly guided the Wei clan to follow Empress Wu's precedent.

sentences.zh: 俄遷尚書左仆射，仍知政事。

translations.literal: Soon he was promoted to Left Vice Director of the Department of State Affairs and still directed government affairs.
translations.idiomatic: He was soon promoted to Left Vice Director of the Department of State Affairs while retaining control of government affairs.

sentences.zh: 帝方南郊，巨源請後為亞獻，而自為終獻。

translations.literal: When the emperor was at the southern suburb sacrifice, Juyuan asked that the empress be secondary offerer and he himself the final offerer.
translations.idiomatic: During the southern suburb sacrifice, Juyuan asked that the empress serve as secondary offerer and he himself as final offerer.

sentences.zh: 及臨淄王平諸韋，家人請避之，巨源曰：「吾大臣，無容見難不赴。

translations.literal: When the Prince of Linzi suppressed the Wei clan, his family asked him to avoid danger. Juyuan said: "I am a great minister—I cannot see difficulty and not go."
translations.idiomatic: When the Prince of Linzi suppressed the Wei clan, his family urged him to flee. Juyuan said, "I am a great minister—I cannot flee from danger."

sentences.zh: 」出都街，亂兵殺之，年八十。

translations.literal: He went out into the capital street and mutinous troops killed him, aged eighty.
translations.idiomatic: He went into the capital street and was killed by mutinous troops at eighty.

sentences.zh: 睿宗立，贈特進、荊州大都督。

translations.literal: When Emperor Ruizong ascended, Juyuan was posthumously given Special Advancement and Great Military Commissioner of Jing Prefecture.
translations.idiomatic: When Emperor Ruizong ascended, Juyuan was posthumously granted Special Advancement and Great Military Commissioner of Jing Prefecture.

sentences.zh: 博士李處直請謚為「昭」，戶部員外郎李邕以巨源附武三思為相，托韋後親屬，謚「昭」為非。

translations.literal: Erudite Li Chuzhi requested the posthumous title "Illustrious." Vice Director Li Yong of the Ministry of Revenue held that Juyuan had attached himself to Wu Sansi to become chancellor and relied on Empress Wei's kin—that "Illustrious" was wrong.
translations.idiomatic: Erudite Li Chuzhi requested the posthumous title "Illustrious." Vice Director Li Yong held that Juyuan had sided with Wu Sansi to become chancellor and relied on Empress Wei's kin—that "Illustrious" was wrong.

sentences.zh: 處直執不改，邕列陳其惡，不見用，然世皆直邕。

translations.literal: Chuzhi held firm and would not change; Yong set forth his evils in detail but was not heeded—yet the age all upheld Yong as right.
translations.idiomatic: Chuzhi held firm; Yong set forth Juyuan's crimes in detail but was not heeded—yet the age upheld Yong as right.

sentences.zh: 韋氏自安石及武後時宰相待價、巨源皆近親，其族至大官者，又數十人。

translations.literal: From Anshi and the chancellors Daizhi and Juyuan in Empress Wu's time, the Wei clan were all close kin; those of the clan who reached high office numbered several tens more.
translations.idiomatic: From Wei Anshi and the chancellors Daizhi and Juyuan under Empress Wu, the Wei clan were all close kin; dozens more of the clan reached high office.

sentences.zh: 趙彥昭，字奐然，甘州張掖人。

translations.literal: Zhao Yanzhao, styled Haoran, was a man of Zhangye in Gan Prefecture.
translations.idiomatic: Zhao Yanzhao, courtesy name Haoran, was a native of Zhangye in Gan Prefecture.

sentences.zh: 父武孟，少遊獵，以所獲饋其母，母泣曰：「汝不好書而敖蕩，吾安望哉？

translations.literal: His father Wumeng in youth roamed hunting and presented his catch to his mother. His mother wept and said: "You do not love books but are wild and dissolute—what can I hope from you?"
translations.idiomatic: His father Wumeng in youth roamed hunting and presented his catch to his mother. She wept and said, "You do not love books but are wild and dissolute—what can I hope from you?"

sentences.zh: 」不為食。

translations.literal: She would not eat.
translations.idiomatic: She would not eat.

sentences.zh: 武孟感激，遂力學，淹該書記。

translations.literal: Wumeng was moved and thereupon studied hard, becoming thoroughly versed in records and writing.
translations.idiomatic: Wumeng was moved and studied hard, becoming thoroughly versed in records and writing.

sentences.zh: 自長安丞為右臺侍卿史，著《河西人物志》十篇。

translations.literal: From Assistant Magistrate of Chang'an he became Attending Censor of the Right Censorate and wrote ten chapters of "Record of Men of Hexi."
translations.idiomatic: From Assistant Magistrate of Chang'an he became Attending Censor of the Right Censorate and wrote ten chapters of "Record of Men of Hexi."

sentences.zh: 彥昭少豪邁，風骨秀爽。

translations.literal: Yanzhao in youth was bold and expansive, his bearing elegant and clear.
translations.idiomatic: Yanzhao in youth was bold and expansive, with elegant and clear bearing.

sentences.zh: 及進士第，調為南部尉。

translations.literal: When he passed the jinshi examination he was assigned as magistrate of Nanbu.
translations.idiomatic: After passing the jinshi examination he was assigned as magistrate of Nanbu.

sentences.zh: 與郭元振、薛稷、蕭至忠善。

translations.literal: He was friendly with Guo Yuanzhen, Xue Ji, and Xiao Zhizhong.
translations.idiomatic: He was close to Guo Yuanzhen, Xue Ji, and Xiao Zhizhong.

sentences.zh: 自新豐丞為左臺監察御史。

translations.literal: From Assistant Magistrate of Xinfeng he became Investigating Censor of the Left Censorate.
translations.idiomatic: From Assistant Magistrate of Xinfeng he became Investigating Censor of the Left Censorate.

sentences.zh: 景龍中，累遷中書侍郎、同中書門下平章事。

translations.literal: In the Jinglong era he was repeatedly promoted to Vice Director of the Secretariat and Associate Grand Councilor.
translations.idiomatic: During the Jinglong era he rose to Vice Director of the Secretariat and Associate Grand Councilor.

sentences.zh: 金城公主嫁吐蕃，始以紀處訥為使，處訥辭，乃授彥昭。

translations.literal: When Princess Jincheng married Tibet, Ji Chune was first made envoy; Chune declined, and Yanzhao was appointed.
translations.idiomatic: When Princess Jincheng married Tibet, Ji Chune was first named envoy; when he declined, Yanzhao was appointed.

sentences.zh: 彥昭顧己處外，恐權寵奪移，不悅。

translations.literal: Yanzhao, considering himself in an outer post, feared power and favor would shift away and was displeased.
translations.idiomatic: Yanzhao, seeing himself sent abroad, feared loss of power and favor and was displeased.

sentences.zh: 司農卿趙履溫曰：「公天宰，而為一介使，不亦鄙乎！

translations.literal: Director of the Court of the Imperial Granaries Zhao Lüwen said: "You are heaven's chancellor yet serve as a mere envoy—is it not base!"
translations.idiomatic: Director Zhao Lüwen of the Court of the Imperial Granaries said, "You are heaven's chancellor yet serve as a mere envoy—is that not base!"

sentences.zh: 」彥昭問計安出，履溫乃為請安樂公主留之，遂以將軍楊矩代。

translations.literal: Yanzhao asked where the plan came from; Lüwen then asked Princess Anle to keep him, and General Yang Ju was substituted.
translations.idiomatic: Yanzhao asked where the plan came from; Lüwen then asked Princess Anle to keep him, and General Yang Ju was substituted.

sentences.zh: 睿宗立，出為宋州刺史，坐累貶歸州。

translations.literal: When Emperor Ruizong ascended, Yanzhao was sent out as prefect of Song Prefecture and, through accumulated guilt, demoted to Gui Prefecture.
translations.idiomatic: When Emperor Ruizong ascended, Yanzhao was sent out as prefect of Song and, through accumulated guilt, demoted to Gui Prefecture.

sentences.zh: 俄授涼州都督，為政嚴，下皆股栗。

translations.literal: Soon he was appointed Military Commissioner of Liang Prefecture; his governance was strict and subordinates all trembled in fear.
translations.idiomatic: He was soon appointed Military Commissioner of Liang Prefecture; his governance was strict and subordinates trembled in fear.

sentences.zh: 入為吏部侍郎，持節按邊。

translations.literal: He entered court as Vice Director of the Ministry of Personnel and held credentials to inspect the frontier.
translations.idiomatic: He entered court as Vice Director of the Ministry of Personnel and held credentials to inspect the frontier.

sentences.zh: 遷御史大夫。

translations.literal: He was promoted to Censor-in-Chief.
translations.idiomatic: He was promoted to Censor-in-Chief.

sentences.zh: 蕭至忠等誅，郭元振、張說言彥昭與秘謀，改刑部尚書、封耿國公，實封百戶。

translations.literal: When Xiao Zhizhong and others were executed, Guo Yuanzhen and Zhang Yue said Yanzhao had shared in secret plotting; he was changed to Minister of Justice, enfeoffed as Duke of Geng with a substantive fief of one hundred households.
