translations.idiomatic: When Xiao Zhizhong and others were executed, Guo Yuanzhen and Zhang Yue said Yanzhao had shared in secret plotting; he was made Minister of Justice, enfeoffed as Duke of Geng with a substantive fief of one hundred households.

sentences.zh: 彥昭本以權幸進，中宗時，有巫趙挾鬼道出入禁掖，彥昭以姑事之。

translations.literal: Yanzhao had originally advanced through power and favor; in Zhongzong's time a shaman Zhao practiced ghost ways and entered the inner palace. Yanzhao treated him as a paternal aunt would.
translations.idiomatic: Yanzhao had advanced through power and favor; under Zhongzong a shaman Zhao practiced occult arts in the inner palace, and Yanzhao treated him with familial deference.

sentences.zh: 嘗衣婦服，乘車與妻偕謁，其得宰相，巫力也。

translations.literal: He once wore women's dress and rode in a carriage with his wife to call together—the shaman's power gained him the chancellorship.
translations.idiomatic: He once wore women's dress and rode with his wife to call on the shaman—it was the shaman's power that gained him the chancellorship.

sentences.zh: 於是殿中侍御史郭震劾暴舊惡。

translations.literal: Thereupon Palace Attendant Censor Guo Zhen impeached him, exposing old evils.
translations.idiomatic: Thereupon Palace Attendant Censor Guo Zhen impeached him, exposing old crimes.

sentences.zh: 會姚崇執政，惡其為人，貶江州別駕，卒。

translations.literal: When Yao Chong held government he hated Yanzhao's character and demoted him to Vice Prefect of Jiang; he died.
translations.idiomatic: When Yao Chong held power he hated Yanzhao's character, demoted him to Vice Prefect of Jiang, and he died there.

sentences.zh: 和逢堯，岐州岐山人。

translations.literal: He Fengyao was a man of Qi in Qi Prefecture.
translations.idiomatic: He Fengyao was a native of Qi in Qi Prefecture.

sentences.zh: 武後時，負鼎詣闕下上書，自言願助天子和飪百度。

translations.literal: In Empress Wu's time he carried a cauldron to the palace gate and submitted a memorial, saying himself that he wished to help the Son of Heaven harmonize the hundred duties.
translations.idiomatic: Under Empress Wu he carried a cauldron to the palace gate and submitted a memorial, offering to help the Son of Heaven harmonize all affairs of state.

sentences.zh: 有司讓曰：「昔桀不道，伊尹負鼎於湯；

translations.literal: The authorities rebuked him: "In old times Jie was without the Way and Yi Yin carried a cauldron to Tang;"
translations.idiomatic: The authorities rebuked him: "In old times Jie was without the Way and Yi Yin carried a cauldron to Tang;"

sentences.zh: 今天子聖明，百司以和，尚何所調？

translations.literal: "today the Son of Heaven is sage and bright and the hundred offices are in harmony—what still needs harmonizing?"
translations.idiomatic: "today the Son of Heaven is sage and bright and the hundred offices are in harmony—what still needs harmonizing?"

sentences.zh: 」逢堯不能答，流莊州。

translations.literal: Fengyao could not reply and was exiled to Zhuang Prefecture.
translations.idiomatic: Fengyao could not reply and was exiled to Zhuang Prefecture.

sentences.zh: 十餘年，乃舉進士高第，累擢監察御史。

translations.literal: After more than ten years he passed the jinshi in the top grade and was repeatedly promoted to investigating censor.
translations.idiomatic: After more than ten years he passed the jinshi in the top grade and rose to investigating censor.

sentences.zh: 突厥默啜請尚公主，逢堯以御史中丞攝鴻臚卿，報可。

translations.literal: The Türk khaghan Mochuo requested a princess in marriage; Fengyao as Vice Censor-in-Chief acting as Director of the Court for Dependencies reported approval.
translations.idiomatic: The Türk khaghan Mochuo requested a princess in marriage; Fengyao as Vice Censor-in-Chief acting as Director of the Court for Dependencies reported approval.

sentences.zh: 默啜遣貴近頡利來曰：「詔送金鏤具鞍，乃塗金，非天子意。

translations.literal: Mochuo sent a noble close attendant Jieli to say: "The edict sent a gold-inlaid saddle set, yet it is only gilded—not the Son of Heaven's intent."
translations.idiomatic: Mochuo sent a noble attendant Jieli to say, "The edict promised a gold-inlaid saddle set, yet it is only gilded—not the emperor's intent."

sentences.zh: 使者不可信，雖得公主，猶非實，請罷和親。

translations.literal: "The envoy cannot be trusted; though we obtain the princess, it is still not real—we ask to end the marriage alliance."
translations.idiomatic: "The envoy cannot be trusted; though we obtain the princess, the alliance is not real—we ask to end the marriage."

sentences.zh: 」欲馳去，左右色動，逢堯呼曰：「我大國使，不受我辭，可輒去。

translations.literal: He wished to gallop away; those at hand changed color. Fengyao shouted: "I am an envoy of the great state—you have not accepted my words; how can you leave at will?"
translations.idiomatic: He wished to gallop away; those present were alarmed. Fengyao shouted, "I am an envoy of the great state—you have not accepted my words; how can you leave at will?"

sentences.zh: 」乃牽持其人謂曰：「漢法重女婿而送鞍具，欲安且久，不以金為貴。

translations.literal: He then seized the man and said: "Han law honors the son-in-law and sends saddle gear, wishing peace and duration—not holding gold as precious."
translations.idiomatic: He seized the man and said, "Han law honors the son-in-law and sends saddle gear for lasting peace—not holding gold as precious."

sentences.zh: 可汗乃貪金而不貴信邪？

translations.literal: "Does the khaghan covet gold and not prize good faith?"
translations.idiomatic: "Does the khaghan covet gold and not prize good faith?"

sentences.zh: 」默啜聞曰：「漢使至吾國眾矣，斯食鐵石人，不可易。

translations.literal: Mochuo heard and said: "Han envoys have come to our state in many numbers; this man who eats iron and stone cannot be changed."
translations.idiomatic: Mochuo heard and said, "Han envoys have come to our state in great numbers; this iron-biting man cannot be changed."

sentences.zh: 」因備禮以見。

translations.literal: He thereupon prepared full ceremony to receive him.
translations.idiomatic: He thereupon received him with full ceremony.

sentences.zh: 逢堯說之曰：「天子昔為單於都護，思與可汗通舊好，可汗當向風慕義，襲冠冕，取重諸蕃。

translations.literal: Fengyao persuaded him: "The Son of Heaven was once Protector-General of the Xiongnu and wishes to renew old friendship with the khaghan. The khaghan ought to turn to the wind and admire righteousness, assume cap and regalia, and win weight among the tribes."
translations.idiomatic: Fengyao persuaded him: "The emperor was once Protector-General of the Xiongnu and wishes to renew old friendship with the khaghan. The khaghan ought to turn toward righteousness, assume cap and regalia, and win esteem among the tribes."

sentences.zh: 」默啜信之，為斂發紫衣，南面再拜稱臣，遣子入朝。

translations.literal: Mochuo believed him, had his hair bound and put on purple robes, faced south and twice bowed calling himself subject, and sent his son to court.
translations.idiomatic: Mochuo believed him, bound his hair and put on purple robes, faced south and twice bowed as subject, and sent his son to court.

sentences.zh: 逢堯以使有指，擢戶部侍郎。

translations.literal: Fengyao, because the mission had purpose, was promoted to Vice Director of the Ministry of Revenue.
translations.idiomatic: Fengyao was promoted to Vice Director of the Ministry of Revenue for the mission's success.

sentences.zh: 坐善太平公主，斥朗州司馬，終柘州刺史。

translations.literal: Punished for siding with Princess Taiping, he was expelled as Secretary in Lang Prefecture and ended as prefect of Zhe.
translations.idiomatic: Punished for siding with Princess Taiping, he was demoted to Secretary in Lang Prefecture and ended as prefect of Zhe.

sentences.zh: 逢堯詼詭，當大事敢僥福，故卒以附麗廢，然唐興奉使者稱逢堯。

translations.literal: Fengyao was witty and crafty; in great affairs he dared gamble on fortune, and so in the end was ruined for clinging to power—yet since Tang's rise, envoys on mission have praised Fengyao.
translations.idiomatic: Fengyao was witty and crafty; in great affairs he dared gamble on fortune and was ruined for clinging to power—yet since Tang's rise, envoys on mission have praised Fengyao.

sentences.zh: 贊曰：異哉，玄宗之器蕭至忠也，不亦惑乎！

translations.literal: The commentator says: Strange! That Xuanzong took Xiao Zhizhong as an instrument—is it not confusion!
translations.idiomatic: The commentator says: Strange that Xuanzong esteemed Xiao Zhizhong—is this not confusion!

sentences.zh: 至忠本非賢，而寄賢以奸利，失之則邀利以喪賢，姻艷後，挾寵主，取宰相，謀間王室，身誅家破，遺臭無窮。

translations.literal: Zhizhong was originally not worthy yet pretended worth for treacherous profit; in failure he sought profit and lost worth. He married the empress's kin, relied on a favored mistress, seized the chancellorship, plotted to divide the royal house—his person was executed, his family destroyed, his stench endless.
translations.idiomatic: Zhizhong was never worthy yet pretended worth for treacherous gain; he married into the empress's kin, relied on a favored mistress, seized the chancellorship, and plotted against the royal house—he was executed, his family destroyed, his infamy endless.

sentences.zh: 而帝以乾曜似之，遽使當國，是帝舉不知至忠之不可用，又不知乾曜之所可用也。

translations.literal: Yet the emperor, because Qianyao resembled him, swiftly made him hold the state—this shows the emperor in promotion did not know Zhizhong could not be used, nor what in Qianyao could be used.
translations.idiomatic: Yet the emperor, because Qianyao resembled him, swiftly put him in power—showing the emperor did not know Zhizhong was unusable, nor what in Qianyao was usable.

sentences.zh: 或稱帝不以罪掩才，益可怪嘆。

translations.literal: Some say the emperor did not let crime obscure talent—how much more strange and lamentable.
translations.idiomatic: Some say the emperor did not let crime obscure talent—how much more strange and lamentable.

sentences.zh: 嗚呼！

translations.literal: Alas!
translations.idiomatic: Alas!

sentences.zh: 力士誠腐夫庸人，不能發擿天子之迷，若曰「至忠賢於初，固不繆於末；

translations.literal: Lishi was truly a rotten, mediocre man who could not expose and pluck out the Son of Heaven's delusion. Had he said, "Zhizhong was worthy at the start and surely not wrong at the end;"
translations.idiomatic: Lishi was truly a mediocre man who could not expose the emperor's delusion. Had he said, "Zhizhong was worthy at the start and surely not wrong at the end;"

sentences.zh: 既繆於末，果不賢於初。

translations.literal: "once wrong at the end, he was indeed not worthy at the start."
translations.idiomatic: "once wrong at the end, he was indeed not worthy at the start,"

sentences.zh: 惟陛下圖之」，如是，帝且悟往失而精來鑒已。

translations.literal: "May Your Majesty consider this"—then the emperor would have awakened to past errors and sharpened future judgment.
translations.idiomatic: "may Your Majesty consider this," the emperor might have awakened to past errors and sharpened future judgment.

sentences.zh: 其後相李林甫、將安祿山，皆基於不明，身播岷陬，信自取之歟。

translations.literal: Afterward making Li Linfu chancellor and An Lushan general—all rooted in lack of clarity; his person cast to the Min mountains—was it not truly self-wrought?
translations.idiomatic: Afterward appointing Li Linfu chancellor and An Lushan general—all rooted in this lack of clarity; his person cast to the Min mountains—was it not truly self-wrought?
